cards.en:
A computer network is an interconnection of computers and peripheral devices (printers, scanners, storage) linked by cables or wireless links. The purpose of a computer network is to exchange information and share hardware and software resources.
Benefits: share files, printers, software and one Internet connection; fast and cheap communication (email, messaging, conferencing); centralised storage makes backup easier; lower overall cost because expensive devices are shared.
Drawbacks: security risks (hacking, malware can spread through the network); cost of network hardware and an administrator; if a key device such as a server or switch fails, many users are affected.
cards.zh:
计算机网络（computer network）是把电脑和周边设备（打印机、扫描器、储存装置）用电缆或无线连接起来。目的：to exchange information and share hardware and software resources（交换资讯、共享软硬件）。
好处：共享文件、打印机、软件和同一条上网线路；沟通快而便宜；集中储存方便备份；昂贵设备共用，总成本较低。
坏处：保安风险（黑客、恶意软件可经网络扩散）；网络设备与管理员的成本；server 或 switch 坏了会影响很多用户。

ex.q: A school has 40 computers but only 2 laser printers. Give TWO benefits of connecting them in a network.
ex.a:
1. All 40 computers can share the 2 printers (hardware sharing), saving the cost of buying more printers.
2. Students can save work to a shared server folder, so files can be backed up centrally and accessed from any computer.
ex.az: 共享打印机省钱；文件集中存放于 server，方便备份，任何电脑都可开启。

cards.en:
A Local Area Network (LAN) is a network that covers a small geographical area such as a home, a school or a small office. A Wide Area Network (WAN) consists of many LANs and covers a large geographical area such as districts and countries; the Internet is the largest WAN.
LANWAN
CoverageSmallLarge
Setup costLowHigh
Data transfer rateHighLow
A LAN is usually owned by one organisation; a WAN normally uses lines leased from telecom companies / ISPs.
cards.zh: LAN：覆盖范围小（家、学校、小办公室），setup cost low, data transfer rate high。WAN：由多个 LAN 组成，覆盖地区或国家，setup cost high, data transfer rate lower；Internet 是最大的 WAN。LAN 通常由单一机构拥有，WAN 多用电讯公司/ISP 的线路。

ex.q: A company has offices in Hong Kong and Shanghai, each with its own network. The two networks are connected. Classify each network and the combined network.
ex.a: Each office network is a LAN (small area, one building). Connecting the two LANs over a long distance via an ISP forms a WAN.
ex.az: 每个办公室是 LAN；两个 LAN 经 ISP 远距连接 = WAN。

cards.t: Misconception: LAN vs WAN is not only about distance
cards.tz: 误解：LAN/WAN 只看覆盖范围
cards.en:
Wrong: “The difference between a LAN and a WAN depends solely on the coverage area.”
Correct: The difference depends on how the devices are connected. Once computers are connected through an ISP, they can form a WAN even in a small coverage area. Because it is extremely difficult to connect computers directly with a cable over a long distance, we usually say a WAN covers a large geographic area.
cards.zh:
错误说法：LAN 和 WAN 的分别只在覆盖范围。
正确：分别在于设备如何连接——once computers are connected through an ISP, they can form a WAN，即使距离很近。只因长距离很难直接拉线，所以一般说 WAN 范围大。

ex.q: Two neighbours in the same building connect their computers through the Internet (via their ISP) to play a game. LAN or WAN?
ex.a: WAN, because the connection goes through the ISP, even though the distance is short.
ex.az: 经 ISP 连接，所以是 WAN。

cards.en:
In a client-server network, a centralised administrative system (server) is present. All resources are stored in a server and shared among the clients connected to it. The administrator controls access to the server and shared resources. A server provides specific network services for other devices; clients are devices that request services from the server. A server is dedicated to running services and is usually more powerful and reliable than a personal computer.
Types: web server (hosts web pages and multimedia; needs large storage), game server (multiplayer games), print server (shares printers), file server, application server (hosts web-based applications such as Google Docs / Office 365 so they need not be installed on each computer; needs high computation power).
cards.zh:
Client-server network：有一个集中管理系统（server），所有资源存在 server，供连接的 clients 共享，由 administrator 控制存取。Server 提供服务；client 是请求服务的设备。Server 专门运行服务，通常比个人电脑更强、更可靠。
种类：web server（放网页，需大储存）、game server（多人游戏）、print server（共享打印机）、file server、application server（如 Google Docs，毋须每部电脑安装，需高运算力）。

ex.q: Is a computer that shares its USB printer with the class AND browses the web a server or a client?
ex.a: Both. When sharing the printer it acts as a print server; when browsing web pages it acts as a web client. The role depends on whether it provides or requests a service.
ex.az: 两者皆是：分享打印机时是 print server，浏览网页时是 web client。

cards.en:
In a peer-to-peer network, devices share resources without a centralised administrative system. All users share their own files, and devices connect with and make requests directly to one another using dedicated software (e.g. BitTorrent). Each device can be both client and server.
Pros: lower cost (no server), easier to set up (no server knowledge), higher flexibility to add or remove devices.
Cons: less secure (no centralised management), dedicated software required, hard to control versions of resources because they are spread over many computers.
cards.zh:
P2P：没有集中管理，设备之间直接分享资源，using dedicated software（如 BitTorrent）。每部设备可同时是 client 和 server。
优点：成本低（不用 server）、容易设置、增减设备灵活。
缺点：较不安全、需专用软件、资源分散难控制版本。

ex.q: Which activity uses a P2P network: (A) browsing a news site (B) watching YouTube (C) downloading with BitTorrent (D) online banking?
ex.a: (C). BitTorrent users download pieces directly from other users' computers. The others use client-server.
ex.az: BitTorrent 是 P2P，其余是 client-server。

cards.tz: 客户端-服务器与对等网络比较
cards.en:
Client-serverP2P
ProsMore secure (user management by administrator); easier to keep resource versions consistent; easier to back up and recover dataLower cost; easier to set up; more flexible to add/remove devices
ConsHigher server setup and maintenance costs; harder to set up and maintain; service stops once the server is downLess secure; dedicated software required; difficult to control versions
Choose client-server for schools/companies needing security and backup; P2P for a few home computers or file sharing at low cost.
cards.zh: Client-server：较安全、版本一致、易备份；但成本高、难设置、server 坏了服务就停。P2P：便宜、易设置、灵活；但不安全、需专用软件、版本难控制。学校/公司选 client-server；家中几部电脑可选 P2P。

ex.q: A 50-staff accounting firm must protect client data and back it up daily. Which architecture? Give two reasons.
ex.a: Client-server: (1) better security through centralised user management and access control; (2) data stored centrally on the server so daily backup and recovery are easier.
ex.az: Client-server：集中管理较安全；数据集中易备份。

cards.en:
Networks provide these services: Internal communications; Conferencing; Resource sharing — file sharing, hardware sharing, software sharing and Internet access service sharing.
Internal communications: computers communicate directly, giving efficiency (communicate without leaving the desk), convenience (no limits as long as you are connected) and privacy (only the intended recipient receives the message). For security, companies send confidential messages through the Intranet rather than the Internet.
cards.zh:
网络服务：Internal communications、Conferencing、Resource sharing（file、hardware、software、Internet access sharing）。
内部通讯好处：efficiency、convenience、privacy。公司为保密，机密讯息经 Intranet 而非 Internet 传送。

ex.q: Why might a bank send internal memos over its Intranet instead of public email?
ex.a: The Intranet is a private network inside the organisation, so confidential information is not transmitted over the public Internet, reducing the risk of interception.
ex.az: Intranet 是内部私有网络，机密资料不经公共 Internet，较难被截取。

cards.en: Conferencing provides real-time collaboration with audio and video communication for users at different locations. Quality depends on the data transmission rate (bandwidth, measured in bits per second, bps). Low bandwidth gives poor audio/video quality, so video signals are usually compressed before being sent. Using a network with a higher data transfer rate improves quality; a higher-resolution camera gives sharper video but needs more bandwidth.
cards.zh: Conferencing：不同地点用户以影音实时协作。质量取决于 bandwidth（bps），带宽低则质量差，所以影片多先压缩。用更高传输率的网络可改善；高解像度镜头更清晰但需更多带宽。

ex.q: A 2 Mbps video stream runs on a 1 Mbps connection. What happens and how to fix it?
ex.a: The stream needs more bandwidth than available, so the video lags, freezes or becomes pixelated. Fix: use a faster connection or lower the video resolution/bitrate (more compression).
ex.az: 所需带宽大于可用带宽 → 卡顿；提升网速或降低解像度。

cards.en:
In a Small Office/Home Office (SOHO) network, files and printers are shared through the network. Administrators create folders on a network server and set access control: read only, read and write, or full control. Users access them as network drives or on a Network-attached Storage (NAS).
Advantages of storing data on central servers: maintains consistency of data for multiple devices; local data can be deleted to save storage space; users can work on the same folder at the same time; facilitates backup; helps recover local data.
cards.zh:
SOHO 网络经网络共享文件。管理员在 server 建 folder 并设权限：read only / read and write / full control；用户以 network drive 或 NAS 存取。
集中储存好处：数据一致、节省本机空间、多人同时工作、方便备份、可还原本机数据。

ex.q: A teacher wants students to submit homework into a shared folder but not see or change others' work. Suggest the access right.
ex.a: Give students write (upload) permission but not read/modify on others' files, e.g. a 'drop box' folder: write-only for students, full control for the teacher.
ex.az: 学生只可写入（上载），老师 full control。

cards.en:
Users share hardware such as printers, scanners and file servers, making full use of hardware and saving cost.
Method A – printer connected to computer A by USB and shared: easy to set up and control, and A can monitor printing quota; but the printer can only be used when computer A is on, and A's CPU/RAM are used so A runs slower while printing.
Method B – printer connected directly to the network with a UTP cable: the printer itself handles authentication, quota and job priority; it does not depend on any computer being on.
cards.zh:
共享 printer、scanner 等可省钱。
方法 A：打印机用 USB 接电脑 A 再共享 → 易设置；但电脑 A 要开机才可打印，且 A 会变慢。
方法 B：打印机用 UTP 线直接接网络 → 打印机自行处理认证与排队，不依赖任何电脑。

ex.q: Give one advantage and one disadvantage of Method A.
ex.a: Advantage: easy to set up and control the printer. Disadvantage: the printer is unusable when computer A is off / computer A runs slower when printing.
ex.az: 优：易设置；缺：A 关机不能打印，或 A 变慢。

cards.t: Software sharing and Internet access sharing
cards.en:
Software sharing: software is installed once on a central server; users take turns to use it via remote logon. This saves software licensing cost and avoids installing on every computer.
Internet access service sharing: one device connected to the Internet shares its connection with others in the LAN. It reduces cost of service and helps monitor and control incoming/outgoing traffic. Examples: pocket Wi-Fi, a Windows PC mobile hotspot (set SSID and password), a phone sharing mobile data via Wi-Fi, Bluetooth or USB.
cards.zh:
软件共享：软件装在 server，用户以 remote logon 轮流使用 → 省 license 费。
上网共享：一部设备分享上网给 LAN 其他设备 → 省费用、可监控流量。例：pocket Wi-Fi、电脑/手机 mobile hotspot（设 SSID 和密码）。

ex.q: A company has 20 staff but only 3 people use video-editing software at any time. How can networking save money?
ex.a: Install 3 licensed copies on a central server and let staff use them via remote logon in turns, instead of buying 20 licences.
ex.az: 在 server 装少量 licence，员工轮流远程使用。

cards.tz: 判断 client-server 或 P2P 服务
cards.en:
To classify a service, ask: is one device providing a service to others (server), or are devices communicating directly as equals?
  • Teacher's desktop shares its printer with all students → client-server (print server).
  • Teacher's desktop shares a folder for homework submission → client-server (file server).
  • A student sends a message directly to another student's desktop using command prompt → peer-to-peer.
cards.zh: 判断方法：是否有一部设备为其他设备提供服务（server），还是设备平等直接沟通。老师机共享打印机/文件夹 → client-server；学生之间直接传讯 → P2P。

ex.q: Two students copy files directly from each other's shared folders with no server. Classify.
ex.a: Peer-to-peer: each computer shares its own resources and they connect directly without a central server.
ex.az: P2P：各自分享，没有中央 server。

cards.t: Network Interface Card (NIC) and MAC address
cards.en:
A Network Interface Card (NIC) allows a device to communicate over a network, using cables or wirelessly. Ethernet NICs have a slot (RJ-45) for an Ethernet cable; wireless NICs usually have antennae, which help to improve signal reception.
Each NIC has a 48-bit unique Media Access Control (MAC) address, used to identify a device connected to a network. It is assigned by the device manufacturer and stored in the hardware, written as 6 pairs of hexadecimal digits, e.g. 00:1A:2B:3C:4D:5E. MAC addresses are also used for security (MAC address filtering).
cards.zh:
NIC 让设备连接网络（有线或无线）。Ethernet NIC 有 RJ-45 插口；wireless NIC 有天线改善收讯。
每张 NIC 有 48-bit 独一的 MAC address，由制造商指定并储存在硬件，用来识别网络上的设备，写成 6 组十六进制，如 00:1A:2B:3C:4D:5E；也用于 MAC address filtering。

ex.q: How many different MAC addresses are possible?
ex.a: MAC address = 48 bits, so 2<sup>48</sup> = 281,474,976,710,656 (about 2.8 × 10<sup>14</sup>) addresses.

cards.en: A switch connects devices to form a LAN and directs incoming data to the destination device based on its MAC address. It is a multiport device: data is only sent out of the port where the destination device is connected, not to every device. Data buffering (data caching) in a switch prevents data collision when several devices send at once.
cards.zh: Switch 把设备连成 LAN，根据 MAC address 把数据送到目标设备；是多端口设备，只把数据送去目标设备所在的端口。Data buffering 可防止数据碰撞。

ex.q: PC1 sends a file to PC3 on the same switch. Which address does the switch use, and does PC2 receive it?
ex.a: The switch reads the destination MAC address (PC3's) and forwards the frame only to PC3's port. PC2 does not receive it.
ex.az: switch 看 PC3 的 MAC，只送往 PC3 端口，PC2 收不到。

cards.tz: 接入点与 Wi-Fi 漫游
cards.en:
An Access Point (AP) connects directly to a wired LAN (normally Ethernet) and provides wireless connection to other devices through Wi-Fi to form a wireless LAN (WLAN). Each AP is identified by its SSID (the public network name). If encryption is enabled, a data encryption key (password) is required. The administrator can limit the maximum number of concurrent users to control traffic and keep performance decent.
Wi-Fi roaming: all APs in the same network should have the same SSID. When a device moves from one AP's coverage area to another's, the wireless NIC disconnects from the original AP and connects to the other AP automatically, so the connection is seamlessly switched. A newer idea is mesh Wi-Fi, where several home routers act as interconnected nodes.
cards.zh:
AP 接到有线 LAN，用 Wi-Fi 为其他设备提供无线连接，组成 WLAN。以 SSID 识别；加密时需密码；可限制同时连线人数。
漫游 roaming：所有 AP 用相同 SSID；设备移动时 NIC 自动由原 AP 转到另一 AP，无缝切换。Mesh Wi-Fi 把多部 router 连成网状。

ex.q: A student loses Wi-Fi when walking from Room 101 (SSID 'School-1') to Room 201 (SSID 'School-2'). Explain and fix.
ex.a: The APs use different SSIDs, so roaming does not happen and the device must reconnect manually. Fix: give all APs the same SSID (and same security settings) so the NIC switches automatically.
ex.az: SSID 不同不能漫游；把所有 AP 设为同一 SSID。

cards.en: A router connects LANs with each other or connects a LAN with a WAN. It forwards incoming data to destination devices based on the IP address. On the Internet, many routers lie between the source and the destination; the main function of a router is to determine the next network node to send the packet to, i.e. choose the path. A home router often combines a router, a switch and a wireless AP in one box.
cards.zh: Router 连接不同 LAN，或把 LAN 连到 WAN，根据 IP address 转发数据。Internet 上源头与目的地之间有很多 router，主要功能是决定下一个节点（选路径）。家用 router 常集 router、switch、AP 于一身。

ex.q: Which device is needed to connect a school LAN to the Internet, and which address does it use?
ex.a: A router; it forwards packets between the LAN and the WAN using IP addresses.
ex.az: Router，用 IP address。

cards.en:
Wrong: “A switch controls the network traffic between different networks.”
Correct: A switch is a multiport device that manages the flow of data in a LAN (using MAC addresses). A router forwards data packets between two networks (using IP addresses).
cards.zh:
错误：switch 控制不同网络之间的流量。
正确：switch 管理 LAN 内的数据流（用 MAC）；router 在两个网络之间转发 packets（用 IP）。

ex.q: Fill in: devices in one classroom connect to a ___; the classroom network connects to another building's network through a ___.
ex.a: Switch; router.
ex.az: switch；router。

cards.tz: 数据机、ADSL/SDSL 与光纤数据机
cards.en:
A modem (modulator-demodulator) is usually provided by the ISP. It converts between the analog signals from the Internet and the digital signals from computers. Modulation combines the digital signal with a carrier wave into an analog signal for transmission; demodulation converts the received analog signal back to digital. Home chain: computer → router → modem → ISP exchange → Internet.
A DSL modem uses traditional copper telephone lines. ADSL (Asymmetric DSL) is mainly for homes: download speed is significantly faster than upload. SDSL (Symmetric DSL) is mainly for businesses: same upstream and downstream bandwidth.
A fibre optic modem (Optical Network Terminal, ONT) converts between light signals and electrical signals.
cards.zh:
Modem（调制解调器）多由 ISP 提供，在 Internet 的类比信号与电脑的数码信号之间转换。Modulation：数码→类比；demodulation：类比→数码。
ADSL：家居用，下载远快于上载。SDSL：商业用，上下行带宽相同。光纤数据机 ONT：光信号 ↔ 电信号。

ex.q: A YouTuber uploads large videos daily from home. ADSL or SDSL?
ex.a: SDSL, because it gives the same high upload speed as download, while ADSL's upload is much slower.
ex.az: SDSL，上载速度与下载一样高。

cards.t: Twisted pair cables: UTP and STP
cards.en:
A twisted pair cable is a group of twisted pairs of copper wires ended by an RJ-45 connector. Twisting reduces electromagnetic interference (EMI) and crosstalk (noise from neighbouring wire pairs). Maximum length is about 100 metres.
ProsCons
UTP (Unshielded, 4 pairs)Lower cost; easier to installShort distance (<100 m); affected by EMI
STP (each pair shielded)Faster than UTP; less affected by EMI, more stableHigher cost; short distance
cards.zh: 双绞线：铜线两两扭绞，两端 RJ-45；扭绞可减少 EMI 和 crosstalk；最长约 100 米。UTP：便宜、易安装，但受 EMI 影响。STP：有屏蔽，较快较稳定，但较贵。

ex.q: A factory floor has heavy machines producing electrical noise. Recommend UTP or STP for 60 m runs.
ex.a: STP: the shielding reduces EMI from the machines, and 60 m is within the 100 m limit.
ex.az: STP，屏蔽可减少机器 EMI；60 米在限度内。

cards.en:
A fibre optic cable is a group of silica (glass) wires that carry data as light using total internal reflection: the core is denser than the cladding, so light hitting the boundary at more than the critical angle is fully reflected along the fibre.
Pros: fastest transmission speed; not affected by EMI so little data loss; less distance restriction; thinner and lighter. Used for WAN links and submarine cables.
Cons: highest cost; hard to install; vulnerable to mechanical damage (bending can break it). A visual fault locator (VFL) shines visible light in; light leaking out shows a break.
cards.zh: 光纤：玻璃纤维以光传送数据，原理是全内反射。优点：最快、不受 EMI、距离限制少、轻薄；用于 WAN 及海底电缆。缺点：最贵、难安装、易受机械损坏。可用 VFL 注入可见光检查是否断裂。

ex.q: Why is fibre, not UTP, used between two campus buildings 400 m apart?
ex.a: UTP is limited to about 100 m, while fibre has much less distance restriction; fibre is also faster and immune to EMI.
ex.az: UTP 限 100 米；光纤距离长、快、不受 EMI。

cards.en:
Satellite can build a network connection in remote areas where wired connection is not accessible (ships, mountains, Starlink). But installation cost and monthly fees are extremely expensive, and stability can be affected by bad weather (rainstorms, windstorms) and sunspot activities; latency is relatively high. Frequency bands are allocated by the ITU.
Microwave needs a straight connection (line of sight) between a microwave terminal and the access point on top of a building; stability is easily affected by the weather.
cards.zh:
卫星：可在没有有线网络的偏远地区连线；但安装及月费极贵，受恶劣天气和太阳黑子影响，延迟较高；频段由 ITU 分配。
微波：需直线视距 line of sight，易受天气影响。

ex.q: A research ship in the Pacific needs Internet. Which link and one drawback?
ex.a: Satellite, since no wired connection is possible at sea. Drawback: very expensive / affected by bad weather.
ex.az: 卫星；但昂贵、受天气影响。

cards.en:
Wi-Fi is a wireless data transmission technology based on IEEE 802.11 standards, using radio waves. Obstacles such as thick walls greatly reduce coverage.
2.4 GHz5 GHz
SpeedSlowerFaster
RangeLongerShorter
InterferenceMoreLess
Microwave ovens, mobile phones and Bluetooth interfere with 2.4 GHz. A dual band router supports both. Wi-Fi 6 (802.11ax) is the latest standard with larger bandwidth and more simultaneous users.
cards.zh: Wi-Fi 以 IEEE 802.11 为标准，用无线电波；厚墙会大减覆盖。2.4 GHz：较慢、范围较远、干扰较多；5 GHz：较快、范围较短、干扰较少。微波炉、手机、Bluetooth 会干扰 2.4 GHz。Dual band router 两者都支援。Wi-Fi 6 = 802.11ax。

ex.q: Choose a band: (a) a laptop next to the router streaming 4K video; (b) a smart plug three rooms away.
ex.a: (a) 5 GHz – faster and less interference at short range. (b) 2.4 GHz – longer range through walls.
ex.az: (a) 5 GHz；(b) 2.4 GHz。

cards.en:
Bluetooth is commonly used for short-distance wireless data transmission between mobile devices (earphones, game controllers, smart bands). It uses radio waves at 2.4 GHz, so it may interfere with 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi. It is extremely popular due to its convenience and high compatibility, has low power consumption and supports peer-to-peer connections. Wi-Fi has a higher data rate, but Bluetooth suits peripherals.
Factors affecting wireless signals: distance, obstacles, interference, weather, direction of antenna. Compared with wireless, a USB cable gives higher data rate, better security and less interference.
cards.zh: Bluetooth：短距离无线传输，用 2.4 GHz（会干扰 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi），方便、兼容性高、耗电低、支援点对点。影响无线信号：距离、障碍、干扰、天气、天线方向。USB 线：更快、更安全、干扰少。

ex.q: Why do wireless earphones use Bluetooth rather than Wi-Fi?
ex.a: Bluetooth has low power consumption (longer battery life), connects directly peer-to-peer with the phone without an AP, and is highly compatible; audio needs little bandwidth.
ex.az: Bluetooth 耗电低，直接与手机配对，毋须 AP。

cards.en:
5G and Wi-Fi 6 provide higher data transfer rates and connect more users and devices to increase network capacity: high throughput, low latency, high capacity.
Bandwidth: the maximum data transfer rate (bps). Throughput: the actual amount of data successfully transferred in a given time; lower than bandwidth because of poor signals, bandwidth bottlenecks and network congestion. Latency: delay for data to travel (ms).
Transfer time = file size (bits) ÷ rate (bps). Remember 1 byte = 8 bits.

cards.en:
Communication software is a network application that runs on end systems and lets users communicate and share resources over a network. Examples: email, instant messaging, web conferencing and even the web browser. Advantages of communicating over the Internet: instant/fast communication, lower cost, supports multimedia messages.

All communication on a network is governed by protocols. A protocol is a set of rules that specify the format and order of the data sent and received between devices. Every device must agree on the same standard. Because the protocol is standardised, devices with different operating systems can still communicate (a Windows PC can load a page from a Linux server). The book compares this to a human protocol: to ask someone the time you use a common language and a polite opening, and you wait for a reply in the expected order.
cards.zh:
通讯软件是在终端设备上运行的网络应用，让用户经网络沟通和分享资源，例如 email、instant messaging、web conferencing，甚至 web browser。用互联网沟通的好处：instant/fast、lower cost、supports multimedia。

网络上所有通讯都受协定 (protocol) 规管：A protocol is a set of rules that specify the format and order of the data sent and received between devices. 所有设备必须遵守同一标准，所以不同操作系统的设备也能互相通讯。书中用“问时间”比喻：要用共同语言、有礼貌地开始、按次序等回应，这就是人类的“协定”。

ex.q: Why can an iPhone (iOS) download a web page from a server running Linux?
ex.a: Both follow the same standardised protocols (TCP/IP and HTTP/HTTPS). A protocol fixes the format and order of the data exchanged, so the operating system of each end does not matter.
ex.az: 双方都遵守同一套标准协定 (TCP/IP、HTTP)，协定规定数据格式和次序，所以操作系统不同也没关系。

cards.en:
The Internet protocol suite is the set of protocols used to transmit data over the Internet. The two most important are the Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) and the Internet Protocol (IP), together called TCP/IP.
TCP: divides the data into smaller packets, numbers them and sends them one by one; when all packets arrive, TCP reassembles them into the original data (using the numbers to restore the order).
IP: responsible for the actual transmission of packets; it adds the source and destination IP addresses to each packet and selects the path — the best path, or an alternative path to avoid network congestion. So packets of one message may travel different routes and arrive out of order.
Four steps: 1 Data division → 2 Use of IP address → 3 Routing → 4 Reassembling.
Why packets? If a packet is corrupted, only that packet (not the whole data) needs to be resent, and different routes share the load.
cards.zh:
Internet protocol suite 是在互联网传数据的一组协定，最重要的是 TCP 与 IP，合称 TCP/IP。
TCP：把数据分成小 packets 并编号逐个送出；全部到达后按编号重组。
IP：负责实际传送，在每个 packet 加上来源及目的地 IP address，并选择路径（最佳路径，或为避开 network congestion 走替代路径），所以同一讯息的 packets 可能走不同路线、不按次序到达。
四步：Data division → Use of IP address → Routing → Reassembling。
为何分 packets？某个 packet 损坏时，只需重传那一个，而不是整份数据。

ex.q: A 5-packet message is sent. Packet 3 arrives corrupted and packets arrive in the order 2,1,5,3,4. Describe what TCP does.
ex.a:
1. TCP detects packet 3 is corrupted and requests only packet 3 to be resent.
2. It waits until all 5 packets have arrived.
3. It uses the packet numbers to reassemble them in the order 1,2,3,4,5 to rebuild the original message.
ex.az: TCP 只要求重传第 3 个 packet，等全部到齐后按编号 1–5 重组。

cards.tz: 五层 TCP/IP 协定堆叠与封装
cards.en:
Data passes through a five-layer TCP/IP protocol stack:
Application layer – interface between the user and the application (browser, email client); data e.g. 'Hello'.
Transport layer – data is divided into smaller packets and a transport header (TH) is added (e.g. which protocol) → segment.
Network layer – a network header (NH) with IP addresses is added; defines which physical path is used.
Data Link layer – maps the IP address to the corresponding MAC address; moves frames between two physically connected devices in the same network.
Physical layer – sends frames as bit streams (1s and 0s) over physical media (cables, radio).
Adding headers on the way down is encapsulation; the receiver strips them on the way up and reassembles the packets: decapsulation (the reverse process).
cards.zh:
数据会经过五层 TCP/IP stack：
Application：用户与应用程式（browser、email client）之间的介面。
Transport：把数据分成小 packets 并加 transport header (TH)（如用哪个协定）。
Network：加 network header (NH)，含 IP addresses，决定实体路径。
Data Link：把 IP address 对应到 MAC address，在同一网络中相连设备之间传送。
Physical：以 bit streams (1 和 0) 经电缆等媒介传送。
发送端逐层加 header = encapsulation；接收端逐层拆除并重组 = decapsulation。

ex.q: At which layer is (a) the destination IP address added, (b) the IP address mapped to a MAC address, (c) the data turned into 1s and 0s?
ex.a: (a) Network layer (network header). (b) Data Link layer. (c) Physical layer.
ex.az: (a) Network layer (b) Data Link layer (c) Physical layer。

cards.en:
IP addresses are changeable numerical addresses used to identify a device in a network under TCP/IP; each IP address must be unique in the network. When a device connects to the Internet, an IP address is assigned by ICANN (Internet Corporation for Assigned Names and Numbers) through your ISP.
Like the addresses on an envelope, each packet carries a source IP address (sender) and a destination IP address (recipient).
IP vs MAC: network devices use the IP address to identify the location of a computer in the network, while the MAC address identifies the computer (NIC) itself. IP is logical and changeable; MAC is 48-bit, set by the manufacturer, and is also used for MAC address filtering. Routers forward by IP; switches by MAC.
On Windows, ipconfig in Command Prompt shows your IP address.
cards.zh:
IP address 是可改变的数字地址，用来在 TCP/IP 网络中识别设备；在网络中必须唯一。连上互联网时，由 ICANN 经 ISP 分配。
每个 packet 像信封一样有 source IP 和 destination IP。
IP vs MAC：IP 识别设备在网络中的位置，MAC 识别设备 (NIC) 本身。IP 是逻辑地址、可变；MAC 48-bit 由制造商写入，也用作 MAC address filtering。Router 按 IP 转发，switch 按 MAC。
Windows 用 ipconfig 查看本机 IP。

ex.q: A laptop moves from home Wi-Fi to school Wi-Fi. Which of its IP address and MAC address may change? Why?
ex.a: The IP address may change, because it is assigned by each network/ISP and shows the device's location in that network. The MAC address stays the same because it is burnt into the NIC by the manufacturer.
ex.az: IP 可能改变（由所在网络分配、表示位置）；MAC 不变（制造商写入网卡）。

cards.en:
An IPv4 address is a 32-bit numerical address formed by four 8-bit numbers (octets) separated by periods. Each octet is 0–255, so the range is 0.0.0.0 to 255.255.255.255. Example: 148.7.52.1 = 10010100.00000111.00110100.00000001.
Total possible addresses = 232 = 4,294,967,296 (≈4.3 billion).
Validity checks: exactly 4 parts, each a whole number 0–255. 192.168.1.256 is invalid (256 > 255); 172.16.1 is invalid (only 3 parts).
Conversion: each octet ↔ 8-bit binary using place values 128 64 32 16 8 4 2 1.

ex.q: Convert 192.168.10.5 to binary.
ex.az: 逐个 octet 拆成位值之和，每段补足 8 位。

ex.q: How many IPv4 addresses exist?
ex.az: 2 的 32 次方。

cards.t: IPv6 and why it was introduced
cards.en:
Most addresses still use IPv4, but IPv4 addresses are soon to be used up due to the significant growth of Internet devices, so IPv6 was introduced to accommodate more addresses.
An IPv6 address is a 128-bit address formed by eight 16-bit numbers separated by colons, written in hexadecimal (each group 4 hex digits). Range 0:0:0:0:0:0:0:0 to FFFF:FFFF:FFFF:FFFF:FFFF:FFFF:FFFF:FFFF. Total = 2128 ≈ 3.4×1038, which is 296 times as many as IPv4.
Example: 2025:1ab1:abcd:1025:20b5:a19a:a315:1212.
cards.zh:
IPv4 因互联网设备急增而快将用尽，所以推出 IPv6 以容纳更多地址。
IPv6 是 128-bit 地址，由八组 16-bit 数字组成，以冒号分隔，用十六进制表示（每组 4 位 hex）。总数 2128，是 IPv4 的 296 倍。
例：2025:1ab1:abcd:1025:20b5:a19a:a315:1212。

ex.q: How many times more addresses does IPv6 have than IPv4?

cards.en:
Two rules:
1. Omit leading zeros in each group: 0f20 → f20, 0db8 → db8, 0000 → 0.
2. Zero compression: one run of consecutive all-zero groups can be replaced by '::'. '::' can appear only once, otherwise the reader cannot tell how many zero groups each '::' stands for. If there are two runs, compress only one, usually the longer.
To expand: count the groups shown, the '::' stands for (8 − shown) zero groups.
cards.zh:
两条规则：
1. 删除每组的前导零：0f20 → f20，0000 → 0。
2. Zero compression：一串连续全零的组可用 “::” 取代，“::” 只可出现一次（否则无法知道各代表几组）。有两串时只压缩一串，通常是较长的。
还原：“::” 代表 (8 − 已显示组数) 个零组。

ex.a:
Step 1 drop leading zeros: 2001:0:0:f20:0:0:0:f10.
Step 2 the zero runs are groups 2–3 (length 2) and 5–7 (length 3); compress the longer: 2001:0:0:f20::f10.
ex.az: 先删前导零，再把较长的一串零（3 组）改为 ::。

ex.q: Expand fe80::1.
ex.az: 已显示 2 组，:: 代表 6 组零。

cards.en:
IP addresses are hard to remember, so we use a domain name: a human-readable and meaningful form of an IP address. Like IP addresses, domain names must be unique on the Internet.
A Fully Qualified Domain Name (FQDN) consists of all domain levels in the DNS hierarchy, each delimited by a period. For www.google.com.: hostname = www, registration name = google, top-level domain = com, and the final '.' is the root domain (usually omitted). What a general user can register is the registration name + TLD (the domain name); the hostname is chosen by the owner freely.
cards.zh:
IP 难记，所以用 domain name：IP address 的易读、有意义形式，同样须在互联网上唯一。
FQDN 包含 DNS 层级中的所有 domain levels，以句点分隔。以 www.google.com. 为例：hostname = www，registration name = google，TLD = com，最后的“.”是 root domain（通常省略）。一般用户注册的是 registration name + TLD；hostname 由拥有者自行设定。

ex.q: Identify the hostname, registration name and TLD(s) of mail.hkuga.edu.hk.
ex.a: Hostname: mail. Registration name: hkuga. Top-level domain: edu.hk (gTLD-type 'edu' combined with ccTLD 'hk'). Domain name = hkuga.edu.hk; FQDN = mail.hkuga.edu.hk.
ex.az: hostname mail；registration name hkuga；TLD edu.hk。

cards.en:
The right-most name is the top-level domain (TLD):
gTLD (generic TLD) – based on the type of organisation: com (commercial), edu (education), gov (government), org (non-profit organisation), net (network provider).
ccTLD (country code TLD) – based on the country or region: hk, cn, jp, uk, au.
Some organisations use both, e.g. .com.hk, .gov.hk, .edu.hk.
Top-level domain registration is accredited by ICANN; names are managed and redistributed by ICANN-accredited registrars (e.g. GoDaddy, HKDNR). The public searches for and registers available names through a domain name registrar.
cards.zh:
最右的是 TLD：
gTLD：按机构类型，如 com、edu、gov、org、net。
ccTLD：按国家/地区，如 hk、cn、jp、uk。
可两者并用：.com.hk、.gov.hk、.edu.hk。
TLD 注册由 ICANN 认可，再由 ICANN-accredited registrars（GoDaddy、HKDNR）管理分配，公众经 domain name registrar 查询及注册。

ex.q: Alan wants www.star.edu.hk, www.star.hk and www.star.com to reach his school. How many domain names must he register? Does he need mail.star.com?
ex.a: He must register 3: star.edu.hk, star.hk and star.com are different domain names (different TLDs). mail.star.com does not need registration: 'mail' is just a hostname under star.com, which he already owns.
ex.az: 要注册 3 个；mail 只是 hostname，不用另注册。

cards.tz: DNS 伺服器与名称解析
cards.en:
A DNS server is used to translate domain names (words) into IP addresses (numbers). This process is called name resolution. Domain names are for humans; computers need IP addresses. The DNS server's location is given as an IP address, usually provided by the ISP; public DNS servers also exist, e.g. Google Public DNS 8.8.8.8.
Analogy: a phone's contact list maps a friend's name to a number; you can also dial the number directly, just as you can type a website's IP into the browser.
nslookup www.google.com.hk (name server lookup) in Command Prompt queries the DNS records. One domain name may map to several IP addresses.
Typical fault: a site opens by IP but not by domain name → the DNS server is out of service/unreachable.
cards.zh:
DNS server 把 domain name（文字）翻译成 IP address（数字），这过程叫 name resolution。域名方便人，电脑需要 IP。DNS server 通常由 ISP 提供，也有公共 DNS 如 8.8.8.8。
比喻：手机通讯录把名字对应电话号码，也可直接拨号＝直接输入 IP。
nslookup 可查询 DNS 纪录；一个域名可对应多个 IP。
常见故障：输入 IP 能开、输入域名不能开 → DNS server 出问题。

ex.q: Ben can open the EDB site by its IP address but not by its URL. Give the most likely reason.
ex.a: Typing the IP works, so the network connection, router and web server are fine. The failure is in translating the domain name to an IP: the DNS server is out of service or the DNS setting is wrong.
ex.az: 网络和 server 正常，问题在 name resolution：DNS server 故障。

cards.en:
A Uniform Resource Locator (URL) identifies a specific location of a resource on the Internet (web page, image, file, video). It usually has four elements:
http://www.example.hk:80/about/network.html
1. Network protocol (http) – the rules client and server both follow.
2. FQDN / IP address (www.example.hk) – a unique identification of a host on a network.
3. Port number (80) – identifies the application on that host.
4. Path (/about/network.html) – location of the resource relative to the root.
cards.zh:
URL 用来识别资源在互联网上的特定位置。通常四部分：
http://www.example.hk:80/about/network.html
1. Network protocol（http）
2. FQDN / IP address（www.example.hk，唯一识别网络上的主机）
3. Port number（80，识别主机上的应用程式）
4. Path（/about/network.html，相对 root 的位置）。

ex.q: Split https://192.168.0.10:8443/admin/login.html into its parts.
ex.a: Protocol: https. Host: 192.168.0.10 (IP address instead of FQDN). Port: 8443. Path: /admin/login.html (folder admin, file login.html).
ex.az: https / 192.168.0.10 / 8443 / /admin/login.html。

cards.en:
More than one application may run on the same host, so a port number identifies a specific application. Analogy: dialling a hotel (IP address) then the room extension (port). Servers listen on specific ports for requests.
If the port is omitted, the browser uses the default port: 80 for HTTP, 443 for HTTPS. Other well-known (reserved) ports: 53 for DNS, (21 FTP, 25 SMTP for reference). A URL like http://site.hk:8080/ forces a non-default port.
cards.zh:
同一主机可同时运行多个应用，port number 用来识别特定应用。比喻：先拨酒店总机（IP），再拨房间分机（port）。
省略时用预设 port：HTTP 80、HTTPS 443；其他 well-known ports：DNS 53。http://site.hk:8080/ 则指定非预设端口。

ex.q: Which port is used by https://www.bank.hk/login and by http://www.bank.hk:8080/?
ex.a: The first omits the port, so HTTPS default 443 is used. The second states 8080 explicitly.
ex.az: 第一个用 HTTPS 预设 443；第二个指明 8080。

cards.en:
A path is the specific location of a resource relative to the root of the web server. In /about/network.html, /about is a folder and network.html is a file inside it. If no file name is given, the browser looks for index.html by default. This is like a file path in File Explorer (root, directories, file extension).
URL validity questions: a URL is invalid if the folder/file it names does not exist in the server's folder structure (wrong folder, wrong extension, file in a different folder).
cards.zh:
Path 是资源相对于 web server root 的位置。/about 是 folder，network.html 是其中的文件。没有文件名时，浏览器预设找 index.html。就像 File Explorer 的路径。
判断 URL 是否有效：看路径中的 folder/file 是否真的存在于该结构中。

ex.q: A server root has index.html and folder news/ containing 2026.html. Which is invalid: (1) http://a.hk/ (2) http://a.hk/news/2026.html (3) http://a.hk/2026.html
ex.a: (1) valid: loads index.html by default. (2) valid. (3) invalid: 2026.html is inside news/, not the root.
ex.az: (3) 无效，文件在 news 资料夹内。

cards.en:
Exam questions often mix address types. Recognise them by format:
IPv4 – four decimal numbers 0–255 with dots (10.0.0.1).
IPv6 – hex groups with colons, may contain '::' (fe80::1).
Domain name – registration name + TLD (google.com).
FQDN – full name with hostname (www.google.com).
URL – protocol + host (+ port) + path (https://www.google.com/maps).
MAC address – six pairs of hex digits, 48 bits (00:1A:2B:3C:4D:5E).
cards.zh: 按格式辨认：IPv4 四个 0–255 十进制数加句点；IPv6 十六进制组加冒号、可有“::”；domain name 如 google.com；FQDN 含 hostname 如 www.google.com；URL 有协定和路径；MAC 六对十六进制数（48 bits）。

ex.q: Classify: (a) 2001:db8::7 (b) ftp://files.ict.hk/a.zip (c) AC:DE:48:00:11:22 (d) www.rthk.hk
ex.a: (a) IPv6 (b) URL (c) MAC address (d) FQDN
ex.az: (a) IPv6 (b) URL (c) MAC (d) FQDN

cards.en:
HTTP is used by the World Wide Web to transfer hypertext documents (web pages) over the Internet. A web (HTTP) server hosts pages; the browser acts as an HTTP client that sends an HTTP request and receives the page in hypertext format.
HTTPS is a more secure version of HTTP that uses Secure Sockets Layer (SSL) encryption (known as Transport Layer Security, TLS). SSL encrypts data during transmission to ensure confidentiality, reliability and privacy; used for trading and private information (online banking). The browser shows a lock and an SSL certificate.
HTTPHTTPS
URL beginshttp://https://
Default port80443
EncryptionNoYes
SecurityUnsecureSecure
cards.zh:
HTTP 用于 WWW 传送超文本文件（网页）。浏览器是 HTTP client，向 web server 发 request，收回网页。
HTTPS 是更安全的 HTTP，使用 SSL（又称 TLS）加密，在传输期间加密数据，确保保密和私隐，用于网上交易、网银；浏览器显示锁头。
HTTP：http://、port 80、不加密；HTTPS：https://、port 443、加密。

ex.q: Why should online banking use HTTPS rather than HTTP?
ex.a: With HTTP, login details and account data travel as plain text and can be read if intercepted. HTTPS encrypts them with SSL/TLS during transmission, so an interceptor only sees unreadable ciphertext; the certificate also helps confirm the bank's identity.
ex.az: HTTP 明文传送，可被截取阅读；HTTPS 以 SSL 加密，截到也读不懂。

cards.tz: HTTP 请求-回应与状态码
cards.en:
HTTP works as a request–response model:
1. The user enters a URL; the FQDN is translated to an IP address by querying DNS.
2. The browser sends an HTTP request to the web server. Common methods: GET requests a resource (e.g. a web page); POST submits data to the server for processing (e.g. a form).
3. The server returns an HTTP response with a status and possibly the resource.
4. When everything arrives, the browser interprets the hypertext and displays the page.
Status codes: 200 OK; 400 Bad Request; 403 Forbidden; 404 Not Found; 500 Internal Server Error; 502 Bad Gateway; 503 Service Unavailable; 504 Gateway Timeout. 4xx = client-side problem, 5xx = server-side problem.
cards.zh:
HTTP 是 request–response 模式：
1. 输入 URL，经 DNS 把 FQDN 转成 IP。
2. 浏览器发 HTTP request：GET 请求资源；POST 把数据提交给 server 处理（如表格）。
3. Server 回 HTTP response（状态码 + 资源）。
4. 收齐后浏览器解读并显示网页。
状态码：200 OK、400、403 Forbidden、404 Not Found、500、502、503、504。4xx 是客户端问题，5xx 是伺服器问题。

ex.q: A user submits a login form and sees '404 Not Found'. Which HTTP method did the form likely use, and what does 404 mean?
ex.a: A login form submits data for processing, so it normally uses POST. 404 means the server could not find the requested resource, e.g. the form's action path is wrong or the page was removed.
ex.az: 表格提交用 POST；404 表示找不到请求的资源。

cards.en:
An email system has user agents (email clients), email servers and email protocols.
SMTP (Simple Mail Transfer Protocol) is used to send emails to the email server; servers also use SMTP to pass mail to each other.
IMAP and POP3 are used by email clients to retrieve emails from the server.
POP3: emails are downloaded to the local computer and organised there; no Internet needed to read them afterwards. By default they are deleted from the server, but clients have the option to keep them.
IMAP: emails are kept on the server; can be organised on the server; changes are synchronised across devices; multiple clients can use the same mailbox; Internet needed to read.
Choose IMAP for multiple devices; POP3 for one designated device and offline reading.
Webmail (Gmail in a browser) is delivered to the browser by HTTP/HTTPS, not IMAP/POP3. Email protocols are background knowledge since the 2019 DSE syllabus change but still appear.
cards.zh:
电邮系统：user agents、email servers、email protocols。
SMTP 用来把邮件发送到 email server（server 之间亦用 SMTP）。
IMAP 与 POP3 用来从 server 收取邮件。
POP3：下载到本机并在本机整理，之后离线也能读；预设会从 server 删除，但可选择保留。
IMAP：邮件留在 server，可在 server 整理，多部设备同步，阅读需上网。
多设备选 IMAP，单一设备离线阅读选 POP3。
Webmail 经 HTTP/HTTPS 送到浏览器，并非 IMAP/POP3。

ex.q: Match the protocol: (a) Outlook sends a message (b) phone, iPad and PC must show the same folders (c) read old mail on a plane without Wi-Fi on one laptop.
ex.a: (a) SMTP (b) IMAP – keeps mail on the server and synchronises (c) POP3 – mail was downloaded to the laptop beforehand.
ex.az: (a) SMTP (b) IMAP (c) POP3。

cards.t: FTP and application protocols on TCP/IP
cards.tz: FTP 与 TCP/IP 上的应用协定
cards.en:
File Transfer Protocol (FTP) transfers files over a network. An FTP connection involves a file server and a client, and user authentication (username and password) is usually required. WinSCP is an FTP client for Windows; FTP is commonly used to upload website files to a web host.
All computers use TCP/IP to communicate on the Internet. HTTP, SMTP, POP, IMAP and FTP are application protocols on top of TCP/IP: they define what the messages mean, while TCP/IP carries them.

所有电脑在互联网上都用 TCP/IP；HTTP、SMTP、POP、IMAP、FTP 都是建立在 TCP/IP 之上的应用协定。

ex.q: Tom wants to upload his website files to a free web host. Which protocol could he use and what does he need?
ex.a: FTP (with an FTP client such as WinSCP or FileZilla). He needs the server address and his FTP username and password for authentication.
